sources.title: Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media
sources.officialRationale: DHS states that replacing duration of status with fixed admission periods for F, J, and I nonimmigrants will provide additional protections, oversight, and opportunities to verify compliance and reduce fraud and abuse.[page:1][web:18]
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: DHS is amending its regulations to change the admission period in the F, J, and I classifications from duration of status to an admission for a fixed time period, and additional changes to admission and extension requirements. This rule has been classified as a major rule subject to congressional review. The effective date is September 15, 2026.[page:1][web:18]
verifiedClaims: The final rule eliminates admission for duration of status (D/S) for F, J, and I classifications and replaces it with admission for a fixed time period.[page:1][web:18]
The rule is classified as a major rule subject to congressional review, with a scheduled effective date of September 15, 2026.[page:1][web:18]

The rule adds transition provisions that allow certain F and J nonimmigrants admitted for D/S before the effective date to remain until the later of their program end date or OPT/STEM OPT EAD end date, capped at four years after the effective date plus a grace period.[page:1][web:18]
The rule shortens the standard F-1 post-completion departure period from 60 days to 30 days for students admitted under the fixed-period system.[page:1][web:18]
sources.verificationNotes: Verified publication, citation, scheduled effective date, major rule status, and core regulatory changes directly from the Federal Register PDF, including DATES, Summary, and regulatory text sections.[page:1][web:18]

sources.title: Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media (Notice of Proposed Rulemaking)
sources.officialRationale: DHS explains in the NPRM that ending D/S and instituting fixed admission periods with extension-of-stay procedures is intended to improve oversight, reduce overstays, and enhance national security.[web:29][web:13]
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: On August 28, 2025, DHS published a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM), Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media.[page:1][web:18][web:29]
verifiedClaims: The NPRM establishing a fixed time period of admission for F, J, and I nonimmigrants was published on August 28, 2025 at 90 FR 42070.[web:29]
The NPRM proposed eliminating D/S and replacing it with a fixed-period admission framework with an extension-of-stay process.[web:29][web:13]
Public comments on the NPRM were collected under DHS Docket ICEB-2025-0001 via regulations.gov.[web:2]
sources.verificationNotes: Confirmed NPRM citation, docket number, and description from Federal Register and regulations.gov.[web:29][web:2]

sources.title: Docket ICEB-2025-0001 (Fixed Time Period of Admission and Extension of Stay Procedure)
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: This final rule provides amendments to the proposed rule covering this topic that was published in the Federal Register on August 28, 2025.[web:2]
verifiedClaims: Docket ICEB-2025-0001 on regulations.gov contains the NPRM and final rule materials for the fixed time period of admission and extension of stay procedure.[web:2]
The docket confirms that the final rule amends the proposed 2025 rule rather than replacing it entirely.[web:2]
sources.verificationNotes: Reviewed the docket landing page to confirm linkage to the NPRM and final rule.[web:2]

sources.title: ICE Duration of Status Regulatory Impact Analysis - Final Rule 2026
sources.officialRationale: The RIA discusses DHS’s view that fixed-period admission with EOS will impose additional costs on students and schools but will enhance integrity and enforcement of inadmissibility and unlawful-presence provisions.[web:15]
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: Immigration and Customs Enforcement Bureau on Jul 17, 2026 Document Details Docket (ICEB-2025-0001) Document Content Download File.[web:15]
verifiedClaims: DHS prepared a Regulatory Impact Analysis for the final rule, analyzing costs over a 10-year period assuming a 2026 effective year.[page:1][web:18][web:15]
The RIA treats the fixed-admission rule as a major rule with significant economic impact.[web:15]
sources.verificationNotes: Located RIA document entry and confirmed its existence and association with the docket; full text not exhaustively reviewed in this pass.[web:15]

sources.title: 8 CFR 214.1 — Requirements for admission, extension, and maintenance of status
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: The passport of an alien applying for admission must be valid for a minimum of six months from the expiration date of the contemplated period of stay.[web:41]
verifiedClaims: 8 CFR 214.1 sets general requirements for admission, extension, and maintenance of status for nonimmigrants, including F and J categories.[web:41]
The regulation ties passport validity to the contemplated period of stay, which interacts with fixed admit-until dates and EOS requests.[web:41]
sources.verificationNotes: Checked current eCFR text for 8 CFR 214.1 to confirm general admission requirements relevant to passport validity and periods of stay.[web:41]

sources.title: 8 CFR 214.2(f) — Special requirements for admission, extension, and maintenance of status for F-1 students
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: Duration of status is defined as the time during which an F-1 student is pursuing a full course of study at an educational institution certified by SEVP for attendance by foreign students, or engaging in authorized practical training following completion of studies.[web:65]
verifiedClaims: Under current regulations, duration of status (D/S) for F-1 students is defined as the period of full-time study or authorized practical training plus authorized time to depart.[web:65][web:63]
An F-1 student admitted for D/S is not required to apply for extension of stay as long as the student is maintaining status and making normal progress to completion.[web:65][web:67]
Program extensions must be requested before the program end date listed on the Form I-20 when a student cannot complete by that date.[web:65]
sources.verificationNotes: Reviewed the current eCFR and authoritative summaries of 8 CFR 214.2(f) for definitions of D/S, program extensions, and OPT/STEM OPT structure.[web:62][web:65][web:67]

sources.title: Unlawful Presence and Inadmissibility
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: Typically, you start accruing unlawful presence if you stay in the United States after the date noted on your Form I-94. However, if you are admitted for duration of status (D/S) and your Form I-94 is marked “D/S”, then you may stay in the United States for the duration of your program, course of study, or temporary work assignment, plus any additional grace periods that may be authorized afterward.[web:61]
verifiedClaims: USCIS guidance confirms that unlawful presence generally begins the day after the I-94 admit-until date for nonimmigrants admitted until a specific date.[web:61]
For nonimmigrants admitted for D/S, unlawful presence generally begins only after status ends and the person remains in the United States.[web:61]
sources.verificationNotes: Reviewed USCIS unlawful presence guidance to confirm the distinction between fixed-date admission and D/S for unlawful-presence timing.[web:61]

sources.title: Optional Practical Training (OPT) for F-1 Students
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: Request that your designated school official (DSO) recommend the OPT. Your DSO will make the recommendation by endorsing your Form I-20 and making the appropriate notation in SEVIS.[web:71]
verifiedClaims: USCIS requires a DSO recommendation in SEVIS and endorsement of Form I-20 before an F-1 student may file Form I-765 for OPT.[web:71]
USCIS guidance specifies filing windows for OPT applications relative to program completion and DSO recommendation.[web:71][web:73]
sources.verificationNotes: Used USCIS OPT guidance to support timing rules for DSO recommendation and Form I-765 filing windows.[web:71][web:73]

sources.title: Optional Practical Training Extension for STEM Students (STEM OPT)
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: Submit the Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization, up to 90 days before your current OPT ... If you file your STEM OPT ...[web:72]
verifiedClaims: USCIS allows F-1 students to file for STEM OPT up to 90 days before the current post-completion OPT EAD expiration, and requires USCIS to receive Form I-765 within 60 days of the DSO STEM recommendation.[web:72][web:79]
STEM OPT extensions are limited to 24 months and have unemployment and reporting obligations defined in USCIS guidance.[web:72][web:69]
sources.verificationNotes: Relied on USCIS STEM OPT guidance and related analyses for filing windows, extension length, and reporting obligations.[web:72][web:69][web:79]

sources.title: DHS Publishes Final Rule Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for F Nonimmigrant Academic Students
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: Once the final rule takes effect on Sept. 15, 2026, nonimmigrants in the F (academic student) category will be admitted to the United States for a fixed period of time instead of duration of status ... not to exceed four years, plus a 30-day period for arrival and an additional 30-day period for departure.[web:53]
verifiedClaims: DHS guidance confirms that, after the rule takes effect, F students will be admitted for a fixed period based on the Form I-20 program length, not to exceed four years, plus 30-day arrival and departure periods.[web:53]
F students admitted for D/S before September 15, 2026 can remain until the Form I-20 program end date or the end of post-completion OPT/STEM OPT, not to exceed November 14, 2030.[web:53]
sources.verificationNotes: Used DHS Study in the States guidance to corroborate Federal Register transition framework and F-1 admission structure.[web:53][web:56]

sources.title: SEVP Governing Regulations for Students and Schools
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: On July 17, 2026, DHS published a final rule establishing a fixed time period of admission and an extension of stay procedure for F nonimmigrant academic students.[web:52]
verifiedClaims: ICE/SEVP acknowledges the July 17, 2026 final rule establishing a fixed time period of admission and EOS procedures for F students.[web:52]
SEVP will be involved in implementing recordkeeping and reporting aspects of the new rule.[web:52]
sources.verificationNotes: Confirmed SEVP reference to the final rule and its role in implementation.[web:52]

sources.title: Duration of Status Explainer
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: D/S allowed F students and J exchange visitors to remain in the country as long as they are making normal progress towards completing their program, rather than to a fixed calendar date.[web:13]
verifiedClaims: NAFSA explains that under the prior D/S framework, F and J nonimmigrants could remain as long as they maintained status, without a fixed admission end date on the I-94.[web:13]
NAFSA summarizes DHS’s stated rationale for ending D/S as concerns about overstays, monitoring capacity, enforcement, and fraud opportunities.[web:13]
sources.verificationNotes: Used NAFSA analysis for contextual explanation of D/S and DHS’s stated rationale; not treated as governing authority.[web:13]

sources.title: Elimination of Duration of Status: Summary & FAQs
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: Beginning September 15, 2026, most F-1 students, J-1 exchange visitors, and their dependents will no longer be admitted to the United States for Duration of Status (D/S). Instead, they will generally receive a specific Admit Until Date (AUD) on their Form I-94 ... admitted until the program or appointment end date shown on the Form I-20 or DS-2019, or four years, whichever is shorter, plus a 30-day grace period.[web:3]
verifiedClaims: Yale OISS guidance explains that after September 15, 2026, new F/J admissions will receive a specific AUD tied to program end date or four years, plus a 30-day grace period.[web:3]

The FAQ describes transition provisions for F-1 students admitted for D/S before the effective date, keeping a 60-day post-completion grace period until travel or EOS converts them to the new system.[web:3]
sources.verificationNotes: Used Yale OISS FAQ to cross-check Federal Register and DHS guidance on AUD calculation, grace periods, transition, and practical implications; not used as primary authority.[web:3]

sources.title: Duration of Status (D/S) Rule Change Frequently Asked Questions
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: Beginning September 15, 2026, most F-1 students, J-1 exchange visitors, and dependents will no longer be admitted for Duration of Status (D/S). Instead, they will receive an Admit Until Date (AUD) on their Form I-94. F-1 students admitted for Duration of Status (D/S) before September 15, 2026, will generally keep the 60-day grace period under the transition provisions until they receive a new AUD.[web:60]
verifiedClaims: ASU guidance confirms that, under transition provisions, F-1 students in D/S before September 15, 2026 retain a 60-day grace period until their status converts to a fixed AUD.[web:60]
ASU clarifies that students entering on or after September 15, 2026 will generally receive a fixed AUD based on program length or four years, plus a 30-day departure period.[web:60]
sources.verificationNotes: Utilized ASU FAQ as corroboration of Federal Register transition and admission rules; not treated as overriding DHS authority.[web:60]

sources.title: New "Duration of Status" Rule
sources.publisher: University of Wisconsin–Madison International Student Services
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: The final rule changes the admission period for F and J nonimmigrants to a fixed period of time ... There will be a 60-day implementation period before the new rule takes effect on September 15, 2026. F and J students and scholars entering the United States on or after September 15, 2026, will receive an AUD on their I-94 matching their I-20 or DS-2019 end date (plus a grace period) or a date four years from entry, whichever is sooner.[web:91]
verifiedClaims: UW–Madison ISS explains that the rule includes a 60-day implementation period before the September 15, 2026 effective date.[web:91]

ISS guidance describes that existing F/J students present before the effective date will transition to a fixed AUD considered to be the I-20/DS-2019 end date or four years from September 15, 2026, whichever is sooner.[web:91]
sources.verificationNotes: Used UW–Madison ISS summary to cross-check transition period and AUD calculation for existing students.[web:91]

sources.title: Presidents Alliance et al. v. DHS Complaint (Duration of Status Final Rule Challenge)
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: The Final Rule has an effective date of September 15, 2026 ... alters the conditions of their nonimmigrant status by, among other things, eliminating the duration of status rule, prohibiting changes in program or academic focus and lateral or reverse matriculation, and, for F-1 students, reducing the grace period for departure from 60 days to 30.[web:94]
verifiedClaims: The complaint in Presidents Alliance et al. v. DHS was filed on August 18, 2026 in the U.S. District Court, challenging the final rule eliminating duration of status.[web:94]
Plaintiffs seek to enjoin implementation of the final rule, alleging violations of the Administrative Procedure Act and other legal defects.[web:94]
sources.verificationNotes: Reviewed complaint to confirm filing date, case name, requested relief, and description of the challenged rule; no TRO or injunction identified as of the research date.[web:94][web:98]

sources.title: Lawsuit challenges US rule ending duration of status
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: The claimants filed a complaint and a motion for preliminary injunction in the US District Court in Massachusetts, seeking to prevent the new rule coming in next month.[web:98]
verifiedClaims: The PIE News reports that a coalition of international education groups and unions filed a complaint and motion for preliminary injunction in Massachusetts to block the new rule ending duration of status.[web:98]
The report reiterates that the rule is scheduled to take effect on September 15, 2026, subject to litigation outcomes.[web:98]
sources.verificationNotes: Used as secondary reporting to corroborate the existence and basic contours of the litigation; primary legal details taken from the complaint itself.[web:98][web:94]

sources.title: DHS Final Rule Eliminating Duration of Status for F and J Nonimmigrants Becomes Effective September 15, 2026
sources.minimalSupportingExcerpt: On July 17, 2026 DHS published a final rule eliminating Duration of Status (D/S) for F and J nonimmigrants. The rule will take effect on September 15, 2026 ... individuals applying for admission in either F or J status would be admitted only until the program end date noted on their Form I-20 or DS-2019 or for 4 years, whichever is shorter, plus a period of 30 days.[web:101]
verifiedClaims: NAFSA reports that the DHS final rule eliminating D/S for F and J nonimmigrants was published July 17, 2026 and is scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026.[web:101]
NAFSA summarizes that under the rule, F/J admissions are limited to the program end date or four years, whichever is shorter, plus a 30-day grace period.[web:101]
sources.verificationNotes: NAFSA analysis used to cross-check DHS and Federal Register statements about effective date and core admission structure; not treated as primary authority.[web:101]
